original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-normal-geometrically-unibranch}
A normal scheme is geometrically unibranch.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 1934 states any normal scheme is geometrically unibranch. The draft does not assume integral, irreducible or Noetherian.
statement: A normal scheme is geometrically unibranch.
conclusions: A normal scheme is geometrically unibranch.

stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 1946 for Noetherian X equates geometric unibranchness with connectedness of punctured spectra of strict henselizations at EVERY nongeneric point of an irreducible component. The excluded generic points are retained.
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is geometrically unibranch (Definition \ref{definition-unibranch}),
\item for every point $x \in X$ which is not the generic point of
an irreducible component of $X$, the punctured spectrum of the
strict henselization $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}^{sh}$ is connected.
\end{enumerate}
conclusions:
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is geometrically unibranch (Definition \ref{definition-unibranch}),
\item for every point $x \in X$ which is not the generic point of
an irreducible component of $X$, the punctured spectrum of the
strict henselization $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}^{sh}$ is connected.
\end{enumerate}

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-number-of-branches-irreducible-components}
Let $X$ be a scheme and $x \in X$. Let $X_i$, $i \in I$ be the
irreducible components of $X$ passing through $x$.
Then the number of (geometric) branches of $X$ at $x$
is the sum over $i \in I$ of the number of (geometric)
branches of $X_i$ at $x$.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 2012 expresses number of (geometric) branches at x as SUM over irreducible components through x of their (geometric) branch numbers. The draft preserves the sum, not product, and indexes precisely components through x.
